verdict.rationale: gstack ships its own delegable agent workflows: specialist personas and skills such as /qa, which iteratively fixes bugs and commits them, and /ship, which runs tests, commits, pushes and opens a PR. A router skill sends any request to the right skill, and community users report delegating work this way. The caveat is that the AI runtime is not built in: the skills run inside a host coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others). missing for 10: a native, self-contained assistant inside gstack itself, independent hands-on verification of the delegation workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: 23 opinionated tools that serve as CEO, Designer, Eng Manager, Release Manager, Doc Engineer, and QA
Sends any gstack request to the right skill (planning, review, QA, shipping, debugging, docs, security, design).
Runs QA testing, then iteratively fixes bugs in source code, committing each fix atomically and re-verifying.
Each supported AI coding agent (Claude, Codex, Factory, Kiro, OpenCode, Slate, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, GBrain) is defined as a typed TypeScript config object
